evals.prompt: I need to start a new CAP project for a helpdesk app. It'll have tickets with a title, description, priority (low/medium/high), status (open/in-progress/resolved), and an assignee. Can you set up the project and write the data model?
evals.expected_output: Correct cds init command, no cds add sample, namespace defined, cuid/managed aspects used, db entity exposed via service projection, PascalCase/camelCase naming conventions followed.

assertions.description: Uses 'cds init <name>' to create the project, not mkdir or bare cds init
Does NOT suggest running 'cds add sample'
CDS model declares a namespace
Uses both 'cuid' and 'managed' aspects from @sap/cds/common
Service exposes entities via 'as projection on' — not raw db entities
Sample data generation uses 'cds add data --records' — not hand-written CSVs

evals.expected_output: Identifies SELECT + conditional as two DB round-trips. Rewrites using a single conditional UPDATE with WHERE clause. Keeps req.reject for error handling.

assertions.description: Explicitly identifies the SELECT + UPDATE pattern as two DB round-trips
Suggests folding the check into a single conditional UPDATE, checking the returned row count
Revised solution still uses req.reject for error handling (not throw)

evals.prompt: I need to make sure the `priority` field in my Tickets entity only accepts values 'low', 'medium', or 'high', and that `title` is required. Should I write a handler for this?
evals.expected_output: Recommends @mandatory for title and @assert.range or a CDS enum/type for priority. Does NOT recommend writing a custom handler.

assertions.description: Does NOT recommend writing a custom handler as the solution
Recommends @mandatory for the title field
Recommends @assert.range or a CDS type/enum for priority validation

evals.prompt: Can you help me build a small todo app in CAP Node.js? I need a Todos entity with a title, a done flag, and an optional due date. Also add a custom action to mark a todo as done.
evals.expected_output: Uses cds init <name>, no cds add sample, namespace defined, cuid+managed aspects, service projection, action registered with srv.on, req.reject not throw, explicit column list in SELECT, cds add data --records for sample data.

assertions.description: Uses 'cds init <name>' to create the project, not mkdir
Service exposes Todos via 'as projection on' — not the raw db entity
Handler uses req.reject() for errors — not throw or req.error
Any SELECT in the handler uses an explicit column list, not SELECT *
Sample data uses 'cds add data --records' — not hand-written CSVs with invented UUIDs

evals.expected_output: Identifies throw new Error as wrong in CAP. Recommends req.reject(400, '...') instead. Explains why: CAP owns error handling, correct HTTP status code, proper OData error body.

assertions.description: Identifies 'throw new Error' as wrong / non-idiomatic in CAP
Recommends req.reject(400, '...') as the correct replacement
Explains why: CAP error pipeline, correct HTTP status code, or OData error body

evals.prompt: In my Tickets entity I have a rule: when status is set to 'resolved', the resolvedAt date must be provided. How should I validate this — do I need a custom handler?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT recommend a custom handler. Uses @assert annotation with a case/when expression, e.g. @assert: (case when status = 'resolved' then resolvedAt end).

assertions.description: Does NOT recommend writing a custom handler as the solution
Uses @assert annotation with a CASE WHEN expression for the cross-field validation
Does not falsely claim that @assert cannot handle conditional cross-field validation

evals.prompt: I need to start a new CAP Java project for a bookshop app. It'll have Books with a title, price, stock (integer), and an association to an Authors entity (name, dateOfBirth). Can you set up the project and write the data model?
evals.expected_output: Correct cds init command with --java flag, no cds add sample, namespace defined in db/schema.cds, cuid/managed aspects used, db entities exposed via service projections, PascalCase/camelCase naming conventions, Maven run from project root, sample data via cds add data --records.

assertions.description: Uses 'cds init <name> --java' to create the project, not a plain 'cds init' without the --java flag
Does NOT suggest running 'cds add sample'
CDS model declares a namespace in db/schema.cds
Uses both 'cuid' and 'managed' aspects from @sap/cds/common
Service exposes entities via 'as projection on' — not raw db entities
All Maven commands (mvn compile, mvn spring-boot:run) are shown running from the project root, not from srv/
Sample data generation uses 'cds add data --records' — not hand-written CSVs with invented UUIDs

evals.expected_output: Identifies multiple issues: (1) CqnReference.Segment does not have a keys() method — use CqnAnalyzer instead; (2) SELECT then UPDATE is a race condition — use .set() with CQN expression for atomic decrement; (3) typed Select returns CdsResult<Books>, not Result; (4) read-modify-write allows lost updates under concurrency.

assertions.description: Identifies that CqnReference.Segment does NOT have a keys() method and recommends CqnAnalyzer
Identifies the read-modify-write pattern as a race condition / lost-update risk
Recommends using .set() with a CQN expression (e.g. s -> s.minus(quantity)) for atomic decrement
Identifies that Select.from(Books_.class) returns CdsResult<Books>, not Result

evals.prompt: I need to make sure the `price` field in my Books entity only accepts values between 0.01 and 9999.99, and that `title` is required. Should I write a @Before handler for this?
evals.expected_output: Recommends @mandatory for title and @assert.range for price. Does NOT recommend writing a custom handler.

assertions.description: Does NOT recommend writing a custom handler for these validations
Recommends @mandatory for the title field
Recommends @assert.range: [0.01, 9999.99] for price validation

evals.prompt: Can you help me build a small bookshop app in CAP Java? I need Books and Authors entities, a CatalogService for browsing, and a custom action 'submitOrder' that decrements stock. Include mock users for testing.
evals.expected_output: Uses cds init --java, namespace, cuid+managed, projections, @Before/@On annotations with typed entity classes, CqnAnalyzer for bound action keys, .set() with CQN expression for stock decrement, ServiceException for errors, spring-boot-starter-security dependency in srv/pom.xml, mock users in application.yaml, mvn compile before writing handlers, mvn spring-boot:run from root.

assertions.description: Uses 'cds init <name> --java' to create the project
Service exposes entities via 'as projection on'
Error handling uses 'throw new ServiceException(ErrorStatuses.XXX, ...)' — not 'throw new RuntimeException' or custom exceptions
Stock decrement uses .set() with CQN expression, not read-modify-write
Adds spring-boot-starter-security dependency to srv/pom.xml for mock auth
Configures mock users in srv/src/main/resources/application.yaml under cds.security.mock.users
Runs mvn compile before writing handler code to generate typed entity classes

evals.expected_output: Identifies two issues: (1) CdsService does not exist — should use CqnService.EVENT_CREATE; (2) throw new RuntimeException is wrong — should use 'throw new ServiceException(ErrorStatuses.BAD_REQUEST, msg)'. Additionally notes that event/entity can be inferred from the method signature.

assertions.description: Identifies that 'CdsService' does not exist and recommends 'CqnService' for event constants
Recommends 'throw new ServiceException(ErrorStatuses.BAD_REQUEST, ...)' instead of RuntimeException
Notes that @Before can infer event and entity from the method signature (List<Orders> parameter implies CREATE + Orders_ entity)

evals.prompt: In my Orders entity I have a rule: when status is set to 'confirmed', the confirmedAt timestamp must be provided. How should I validate this in CAP Java — do I need a custom handler?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT recommend a custom handler. Uses @assert annotation with a case/when expression for cross-field validation.

assertions.description: Does NOT recommend writing a custom handler as the primary solution
Uses @assert annotation with a CASE WHEN expression for cross-field validation
Does not falsely claim that @assert cannot handle conditional cross-field validation

evals.prompt: I'm trying to run my CAP Java app but getting errors. I'm running `mvn spring-boot:run -pl srv` from the project root. Also, to check if the app is up I'm curling http://localhost:8080/odata/v4/ — it returns 404. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies two problems: (1) '-pl srv' triggers ReactorModuleConvergence failure — must run 'mvn spring-boot:run' from project root without -pl; (2) /odata/v4/ always returns 404 — must poll an actual entity endpoint like /odata/v4/<service>/<Entity> for health check.

assertions.description: Identifies that '-pl srv' or running from srv/ directory will cause ReactorModuleConvergence failure
Recommends 'mvn spring-boot:run' from project root without -pl flag
Explains that /odata/v4/ root always returns 404 and is NOT a valid health-check endpoint
Recommends polling an actual entity endpoint (e.g. /odata/v4/browse/Books) to verify readiness

evals.expected_output: Identifies that CqnReference.Segment does not have a keys() method. Recommends using CqnAnalyzer.create(context.getModel()) and analyzer.analyze(context.getCqn()) to extract targetKeys().

assertions.description: Identifies that CqnReference.Segment does NOT have a keys() method
Recommends CqnAnalyzer.create(context.getModel()) for extracting keys
Shows calling analyzer.analyze(context.getCqn()).targetKeys() to get the bound entity's key values
